title: Effectiveness of Generate–Validate–Repair (GVR) Pipelines with Deterministic Verifiers under Distribution Shift and Adversarial Prompts — Preregistration (Repaired)
research_question: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline reduce the rate of unsafe configuration applications by LLM-based NetOps agents under matched in-distribution, distribution-shift, and adversarial-prompt conditions, compared to an LLM-only pipeline, when executed as a paired, emulation-grounded benchmark?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The paired unsafe-apply rate (fraction of tasks where a configuration would produce a semantic safety violation when applied) is lower for the GVR arm than for the LLM-only arm. (Estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline).

H2 (shift interaction): Under distribution-shift tasks (novel topologies/vendors), the absolute reduction in unsafe-apply rate from GVR remains positive and statistically significant but is smaller than the in-distribution reduction.

H3 (adversarial interaction): Adversarial prompt injections cause more repair iterations in the GVR arm (higher median repair count), but the GVR arm still yields fewer unsafe applications than LLM-only.
exploratory_questions: E1: How does the average repair-iteration count and total model-call budget differ by condition (in-distribution / shift / adversarial)?
E2: How sensitive are results to verifier-check subsets (ablation over verifier-check classes)?
E3: How stable are effects across two hosted LLM providers (sensitivity analysis)?
benchmark_scope: Emulation-grounded NetConfArena-style closed-loop testbed (synthetic multi-vendor device images and hidden executable tests) — tasks limited to the supplied emulation environment and synthetic device images drawn from the public test corpus referenced in evidence.
Task corpus is limited to intent-to-configuration conversion tasks described in the preregistration; claims are explicitly bounded to this benchmark scope.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired difference in unsafe-apply rate: GVR minus LLM-only)
secondary_estimands: Per-condition unsafe-apply rates (GVR and LLM-only) with 95% bootstrap CIs
Median repair-iteration count per arm per condition
Total model calls consumed per task and per arm
Latency buckets distribution per arm (interactive <2s, near-real-time <30s, async)
sampling_plan: Paired design with exactly N = 240 distinct intents/tasks. Each task is executed under both arms (baseline/LLM-only and guarded/GVR) using the registered adapter behavior. Task composition: In-distribution = 60% (144 tasks), Distribution-shift = 20% (48 tasks; novel topologies/vendors held-out from the task generator), Adversarial-prompt = 20% (48 tasks; adversarial prompts generated and blinded per preregistered adversary procedure). Tasks are blocked into 24 topology-vendor clusters. For each intent both conditions are executed (paired); the adapter requires one shared initial generation per task and up to one repair call for guarded items. Runtime LLM sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, seed metadata as provided by the hosted model API) will be recorded for every model call. The registered adapter's shared_initial_candidate semantics means a single initial generation is produced per task and reused across the paired episodes; this is not a claim of deterministic LLM sampling—sampling nondeterminism is possible and is documented in execution logs.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned N=240 pairs. Target detectable effect: absolute reduction of 8 percentage points (e.g., from 20% to 12%) with alpha=0.05 two-sided; approximate power >80% under stated baseline assumptions. Exact effect estimates, bootstrap 95% CIs, and exact p-values will be produced by the registered 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' executor at analysis time. If realized baseline rates differ materially, the exact minimum detectable effect will be reported post hoc.
exclusion_rules: Exclude pairs where verifier–simulator inconsistency is detected and flagged as 'possible false-safe' from the primary analysis (these are reported and included in predeclared sensitivity analyses).

Exclude task pairs with unrecoverable infrastructure failures after the preregistered retry policy (primary analysis follows 'complete_pair_primary' exclusion; all such exclusions are reported and included in sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe).
missingness_plan: Retry policy: deterministic automatic reruns for infra failures up to 2 attempts. If both attempts fail, mark the pair as infra-failed. Primary analysis excludes infra-failed pairs per the registered-adapter 'complete_pair_primary' treatment; a sensitivity analysis will treat these failed pairs as unsafe (failure-as-zero). All missingness counts and root causes will be reported in the execution manifest.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis uses the registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' (estimand id: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) to estimate the paired unsafe-apply rate difference (GVR minus LLM-only). Binary outcome per task: unsafe_apply (1) vs safe_apply (0) determined by deterministic simulation after the arm's final output (for GVR: after up-to-1 repair per adapter contract). Report risk difference, 95% bootstrap CIs, and exact p-value from the registered executor. Stratified per-condition analyses (in-distribution, shift, adversarial) use the same paired executor. Repair-iteration counts compared with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (reported as secondary analyses). Latency comparisons use Wilcoxon or paired t-test depending on distributional checks. Failed-call treatments per executor options: primary = complete_pair_primary; sensitivity = complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity. All analysis code, runtime seeds/recorded sampling parameters, and raw results will be archived.
multiplicity_plan: Single primary hypothesis (H1). Secondary hypotheses and exploratory tests reported with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction for secondary tests; report both uncorrected and corrected p-values. All subgroup and post hoc tests labeled exploratory.

stopping_rule: No early stopping for efficacy. Stop after completing all preregistered task pairs (N=240) or if the registered execution adapter's maximum_model_calls limit (exactly task_count * 2 = 480) is reached. Technical retries allowed per task for infra failures up to 2 attempts; no reruns to change scientific outcomes beyond this policy.
